problem: The heading reverses the verse's order (ਗਉੜੀ · ਸੁਖਮਨੀ · ਮਃ ੫). Nothing in English grammar requires this, and the opening should model the line-by-line order. Minor.
fix: Raag Gauri: Sukhmani, by the Fifth Guru.

problem: ੴ is ੧ + ਓਅੰਕਾਰ. 'God is One' renders only the ੧. Oankar (the one all-pervading Creator: our glossary has 'the One Universal Creator') is lost. This is the work's first line, so it should be complete.
fix: Salok. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Salutation to the Primal Guru, who was before all. Salutation to the Guru who has been since the ages began. Salutation to the True Guru. Salutation to the revered, divine Guru.

problem: 'Let me remember God in Simran (meditative remembrance of God)' says remembering twice (remember … in remembrance). ਸਿਮਰਉ is simply 'let me remember / do Simran'. 'and so' adds a causal link the verse lacks (line 2 is a second wish, as in our Hindi: और). 'The one in whose heart …, his glory cannot be counted' is not a grammatical English sentence.
fix: Ashtapadi. Let me practise Simran (meditative remembrance of God) and, remembering him again and again, find peace and rid my body of strife and anguish. Let me remember the One, the Sustainer of the universe, whose Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is repeated by multitudes beyond counting. The Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis, pure words all, were made from the one word of the Lord's Name. The one in whose heart God places even a particle of it has glory beyond counting. Some long for one thing only, the sight of you; says Nanak, save me along with them.

problem: ਪ੍ਰਭ ਕੈ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ ਜਪ ਤਪ ਪੂਜਾ: the sense (our Hindi: स्मरणमें ही जप, तप और पूजा है) is that Simran is itself the chanting, austerity and worship, which it surpasses. 'Through Simran of God come chanting, austerity and worship' tells the reader that Simran leads to ritual practices, the opposite of the Gurmat point. Write it as an equivalence, like the writer's own ਤੀਰਥ ਇਸਨਾਨੀ line ('one has bathed …').
fix: Through Simran of God come riches, spiritual powers and the nine treasures. Through Simran of God come knowledge, meditation and insight into the essence. Through Simran of God, one has performed chanting, austerity and worship. Through Simran of God, duality is destroyed. Through Simran of God, one has bathed at the places of pilgrimage. Through Simran of God, one is honoured in God's court. Through Simran of God, whatever happens is good. Through Simran of God, life bears its fruit in full. They alone practise Simran whom God himself moves to it. Says Nanak, I fall at their feet.

problem: (1) ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨੁ ਕਰਿ (the devotees did Simran) is rendered with the locative refrain 'Through Simran of the Lord'. The writer's own refrains sheet gives 'By practising Simran of the Lord,' for this phrase. 'his' devotees is not in the verse. (2) The last sentence, 'The one whom … has, says Nanak, received Simran of the Lord as a Gurmukh', splits its verb and is hard to read. The ਤਿਨਿ … ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ reading (that Gurmukh), as in our Hindi, reads more simply.
fix: By practising Simran of the Lord, the devotees became renowned. Absorbed in Simran of the Lord, the sages brought forth the Vedas. Through Simran of the Lord, people became Siddhas, celibates and givers. Through Simran of the Lord, the lowly became known in all four directions. Through Simran of the Lord, the whole earth is upheld. Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes. Through Simran of the Lord, all visible creation was made. In Simran of the Lord, the Formless One himself is present. When God, in his grace, has himself given someone understanding, says Nanak, that Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) has received Simran of the Lord.

problem: ਜਹ ਮਹਾ ਭਇਆਨ ਦੂਤ ਜਮ ਦਲੈ: the verb ਦਲੈ is singular, so it is the messenger of Death, not 'messengers'. ਮਹਾ (very, most) is dropped. Minor.
fix: Ashtapadi. Where there is no mother, father, son, friend or brother, there, O mind, the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) is with you to help you. Where the most dreadful messenger of Death would crush you, there the Naam alone goes along with you. Where the hardship is very heavy, the Lord's Naam rescues you in an instant. Performing countless rites of atonement, one does not cross over; the Lord's Naam drives away millions of sins. O my mind, repeat the Naam as a Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru); says Nanak, you will find joys in abundance.

problem: 'The one who thirsts for the sight of God, says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to him' is not a grammatical English sentence: the opening noun phrase has no verb.
fix: If anyone asks for the four great blessings of life, let him take up the service of the holy. If anyone would erase his own sorrow, let him sing the Naam, Har Har, in his heart always. If anyone longs for honour for himself, let him give up this Haumai in the Saadh Sangat (the fellowship of the holy). If anyone fears birth and death, let him seek the refuge of the holy. To the one who thirsts for the sight of God, says Nanak, I am a sacrifice, again and again.

problem: Exclamation mark. Style §5 allows one only where the verse exclaims (ਜੈ, ਧੰਨ, ਹਾ). ਕਵਨ ਮੂਲ ਤੇ ਕਵਨ ਦ੍ਰਿਸਟਾਨੀ is a rhetorical statement, not an exclamation.
fix: Ashtapadi. O mortal, call to mind the virtues of the all-pervading Lord: from what beginning he has brought you to how you now appear. He fashioned you, shaped you and adorned you; he kept you safe in the fire of the womb; in childhood he fed you with milk; in the fullness of youth, food, comfort and understanding; when you grew old, kin and friends were there to tend you and put food into your mouth as you sat. This worthless one does not appreciate any of these kindnesses; should you, Lord, forgive him, says Nanak, then he wins through.

problem: Two sentences begin with a dangling noun phrase and pick it up again with a pronoun ('The one who protects …, the ignorant fool does not love him'; 'The Master who is ever … present, the blind man thinks him far away'). Neither is grammatical English. Rewriting them on the pattern the writer already uses in lines 3 to 4 and 7 to 8 ('…, yet …') keeps the line order.
fix: God is the protector from the beginning to the end, yet the ignorant fool does not love him. Serving him one obtains the nine treasures, yet the fool does not set his mind on him. The Master is ever and always present, yet the blind man thinks him far away. Serving him one is honoured in God's court, yet the ignorant simpleton forgets him. Forever and ever this mortal goes astray; says Nanak, the Protector is infinite.

problem: ਬੇਨਤੀ ਕਰੈ … ਤਰੈ: what is prayed for is a wish (may Nanak cross over). 'makes his prayer: Nanak crosses over by your grace' turns it into a statement of fact.
fix: How can a blind man find the road by hearing alone? Take him by the hand, and he is carried through to the end. How can the deaf understand a riddle? Say night, and he takes it for day. How can the mute sing hymns to the Lord? Even if he tries, his voice breaks. How can the lame roam about on a mountain? He cannot go there. O Creator, full of compassion, this humble one makes his prayer: may Nanak cross over by your grace.

problem: 'One to whose mind God seems sweet, in his mind all joys come to dwell' is not grammatical English: it has a dangling subject and a repeated 'mind'.
fix: Ashtapadi. He takes ten things and puts them out of mind; for the sake of one thing, he throws away his good faith. If God gave not even that one, and took away the ten as well, then tell me, what could the fool do? The Master against whom no one has any power, to him one should always bow. When God seems sweet to someone's mind, all joys come to dwell in that mind. The servant whom God brings to accept his Hukam (his will), says Nanak, has obtained all things.

problem: 'One who gives his love to a passing traveller, nothing comes into his hands' has a dangling subject and is not grammatical English.
fix: Attachments to Maya, the world's lure, are of countless kinds; know that they are sure to pass away. One falls in love with the shade of a tree; the shade passes, and he regrets it in his mind. Whatever is seen will pass away; yet one utterly blind clings to it. One who gives his love to a passing traveller is left with nothing in his hands. O mind, love of the Lord's Naam brings peace; says Nanak, God in his grace himself attaches one to it.

problem: Gobind is not glossed in Ashtapadi 5. It was glossed in a03.p4, and the refrains sheet and §12 say to gloss once per ashtapadi.
fix: Wasted is the life of the Saakat, the faithless one turned from God. Without the True One, how can anyone be pure? Wasted is the body of the blind without the Naam; a foul smell comes from his mouth. Without Simran (meditative remembrance of God), day and night pass in waste, as a crop is lost without rain. Without devotion to Gobind, the Lord of the universe, all deeds are wasted, like the useless money of a miser. Blessed, blessed are those people in whose hearts the Lord's Name dwells; says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to them, again and again.

problem: 'One within whom the Formless Lord dwells, by his teaching the world crosses over' has a dangling subject and is not grammatical English.
fix: His way of life is one thing, and what he practises is another. In his mind there is no love, yet his mouth spins tall talk. God, the Knower, is wise in all things; he is not won over by anyone's outward garb. One who preaches to others but does not practise it himself keeps coming and going, being born and dying. When the Formless Lord dwells within someone, by his teaching the world crosses over. Those who please you have known God; Nanak falls at the feet of those people.

problem: Ambiguous. 'He alone is a servant on whom he has shown grace' comes straight after six sentences in which 'He' is God, so the reader takes it as 'God alone is a servant'. ਸੋ ਸੇਵਕੁ means 'that one (the person) is the servant'.
fix: I offer my prayer to the Supreme Lord, who knows everything. He himself honours what he has made. He himself, all by himself, settles every matter. To some he makes himself seem far away; to others he shows that he is near. He is beyond all devices and cleverness. He knows everything about the soul's way of living. Whomever he pleases, he attaches to the hem of his robe. He pervades every place and every space between. That one alone is a servant on whom God has shown grace. Says Nanak, repeat the Lord's Name at every instant.

problem: ਤੇਰਾ ਓਲਾ ਰਹਤ (glossary: cover, honour; our Hindi: पर्दा, लाज): 'your modesty stays covered' is an odd collocation that suggests clothing. The sense is that your honour stays sheltered.
fix: By whose grace your body is healthy and golden, attune yourself in love to that Lord, your loving friend. By whose grace your honour stays shielded, O mind, you will find peace in telling the praise of Har Har. By whose grace all your faults are covered, O mind, seek the refuge of that God, the Master. By whose grace no one can equal you, O mind, remember the lofty God with every breath. By whose grace you obtained this body, so hard to obtain, says Nanak, worship him with devotion.

problem: 'When God is well pleased, that God makes his home in the mind': 'that God' reads as one god among others. ਸੋਇ is simply 'he'.
fix: He whom God himself moves to repeat it repeats the Name. He whom God himself moves to sing sings the praises of the Lord. Through God's grace, light dawns within. Through God's mercy, the lotus of the heart blossoms. When God is well pleased, he makes his home in the mind. Through God's mercy, the intellect becomes sublime. All treasures, O God, lie in your mercy. By their own effort no one has gained anything. To whatever you attach them, to that they are attached, O Lord and Master; says Nanak, nothing is in their own hands.

problem: Partly disagree. ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: ਜਪੈ is third person singular (glossary: chants), ਜਾਪੁ is its object, and ਜਪੁ is the imperative. 'says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone' drops the third-person clause. It also differs from the writer's own treatment of the third-person verbs ਬੋਲੈ (a03.p4) and ਕਹੈ (a06.p5), which the writer renders 'Nanak utters …', 'Nanak speaks …' and uses to correct our Hindi. The owner should choose one treatment for all three.
fix: {"id": "a06.p7", "issue": "ਨਾਨਕ ਜਾਪੁ ਜਪੈ ਜਪੁ ਸੋਇ: ਜਪੈ is 3rd person singular (Nanak chants the chant), ਜਪੁ imperative, ਸੋਇ 'that very One'. Same question as ਬੋਲੈ (a03.p4) and ਕਹੈ (a06.p5): indicative 'Nanak repeats' or hortative 'let one repeat'.", "our reading": "By whose grace all are liberated, Nanak repeats his Name; repeat the Name of that very One.", "alternatives": "says Nanak, repeat his Name, and his alone (writer; our Hindi 'हे नानक! उसीका जाप जपो'); hortative throughout: 'let one repeat …' here, and likewise in a03.p4 and a06.p5"}

problem: Agree with the writer's doubt (ਸਿਮਰਨਿ is instrumental/locative, and the agent of the perfect participles ਧਾਰੀ and ਕੀਓ; 'for the sake of' has no basis in the form). Supplying 'the sages' for ਉਪਾਏ is a fair implied agent. One more line needs recording: ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਕਾਰਨ ਕਰਨਾ is rendered as an imperative, but every other line of the pauri states what Simran has done. ਸਿਮਰਿ can also be the conjunctive participle ('by remembering again and again'), and some commentaries read the line that way.
fix: {"id": "a01.p8", "issue": "ਸਿਮਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਿ ਹਰਿ ਕਾਰਨ ਕਰਨਾ: imperative (remember, remember the Lord) or conjunctive participle in a pauri of statements (by remembering again and again, one becomes one with the Lord, the Cause of causes)?", "our reading": "Remember, remember the Lord, the Maker of all causes (as our Hindi, which adds हे मन).", "alternatives": "Remembering him again and again, one becomes one with the Lord, the Maker of all causes (the participle reading; 'becomes one with' is implied, not in the words)."}

problem: Agree with the writer. ਹਰਿ ਸਿਮਰਨਿ (instrumental, the agent of ਧਾਰੀ and ਕੀਓ) means 'by / through Simran', not 'for the sake of Simran' (के लिये), in lines 5 and 7. Also: 'हे मन!' in line 6 is not in the verse (no ਮਨ). In the last line ਬੁਝਾਇਆ is past (समझ दी है).
fix: हरिका स्मरण करके भक्त प्रकट (प्रसिद्ध) हुए। हरिके स्मरणमें लगकर वेद रचे गये। हरिके स्मरणसे लोग सिद्ध, यती और दानी बने। हरिके स्मरणसे नीच भी चारों दिशाओंमें प्रसिद्ध हो गये। हरिके स्मरणसे ही सारी धरती टिकी हुई है। जगत्‌के कर्ता और कारण हरिका बार-बार स्मरण करो। हरिके स्मरणसे ही सारा आकार (सृष्टि) रचा गया। हरिके स्मरणमें निराकार प्रभु स्वयं बसता है। जिसे उसने कृपा करके स्वयं समझ दी है, हे नानक! उसी गुरुमुखने हरिका स्मरण पाया है।

problem: Agree with the writer. ਹੈਵਰ is हयवर, the finest horses (MW: haya, horse; the parallel गजवर is 'the choicest of elephants'). Elephants would be ਗੈਵਰ. Our glossary already has 'श्रेष्ठ घोड़े (हयवर)'.
fix: कोई पृथ्वीके नौ खण्डोंमें घूमे और बहुत लम्बा जीये; महान् विरक्त और तपस्वी बन जाय; अग्निमें अपने प्राणोंका होम कर दे; सोना, घोड़े, उत्तम घोड़े और भूमि दान करे; निउली-कर्म करे और बहुत-से आसन करे; जैन-मार्गके संयम और कठोर साधन करे; शरीरको रत्ती-रत्ती करके कटवा दे — तब भी अहंकारका मैल नहीं जाता। हरिके नामके बराबर कुछ नहीं है। हे नानक! गुरुके सम्मुख होकर नाम जपनेसे (जीव) मुक्ति पाते हैं।

problem: Agree with the writer. ਬੋਲੈ is third person singular (Nanak says it), not an imperative. The Hindi also drops ਸੁਭਾਇ (with love).
fix: बहुत चतुराई करनेपर भी यमका भय व्यापता है। अनेक यत्न करनेपर भी तृष्णा तृप्त नहीं होती। अनेक भेष धारण करनेसे भी (तृष्णाकी) आग नहीं बुझती। करोड़ों उपाय करनेपर भी प्रभुके दरबारमें स्वीकार नहीं होता। मोहमें और मायाके जालमें फँसा जीव आकाशमें या पातालमें भागकर भी नहीं छूटता। अन्य सारी करनियोंको यम दण्ड देता है; गोविन्दके भजनके बिना वह तिलभर भी नहीं मानता। हरिका नाम जपनेसे दुःख चला जाता है। नानक सहज अवस्थामें प्रेमपूर्वक वही नाम बोलता है।

problem: Agree with the writer (from the doubts file; this item is not in the list in the task, but the writer says our Hindi is wrong here). In ਜੋ ਤੁਮ ਭਾਨੇ ਤਿਨ ਪ੍ਰਭੁ ਜਾਤਾ, ਪ੍ਰਭੁ (with aunkar) is the object, not a vocative. They have known God, not 'you'.
fix: (मनुष्य) रहता किसी और ढंगसे है और कमाता कुछ और है। मनमें प्रीति नहीं, पर मुँहसे बड़ी-बड़ी बातें गाँठता है। जाननेवाला प्रभु चतुर (सर्वज्ञ) है; वह बाहरी भेषसे किसीपर रीझता नहीं। जो दूसरोंको उपदेश देता है पर स्वयं नहीं करता, वह आता-जाता, जन्मता-मरता रहता है। जिसके भीतर निराकार प्रभु बसता है, उसकी सीखसे संसार तर जाता है। जो तुम्हें भाये, उन्होंने ही प्रभुको जाना है। नानक उन जनोंके चरणों पड़ता है।

problem: Agree with the writer. ਕਰਉ is first person singular (I pray), not an imperative.
fix: मैं उस पारब्रह्मसे विनती करता हूँ, जो सब जानता है। अपने रचे हुए (जीवों) का वह आप ही आदर करता है। वह आप ही अपने-आप निर्णय करता है। किसीको वह दूर जान पड़ता है, किसीको पास समझ आता है। वह सब उपायों और चतुराइयोंसे परे है। वह आत्माकी सारी रहनी (दशा) जानता है। जिसे वह चाहता है, उसे अपने पल्लेसे लगा लेता है। वह सब स्थानों और स्थानोंके बीच समाया हुआ है। वही सेवक है जिसपर उसने कृपा की है। हे नानक! क्षण-क्षण हरिको जपो।

problem: Agree with the writer. ਕਹੈ is third person singular (Nanak speaks his praise), not an imperative. See also the a06.p7 doubt about treating these third-person verbs consistently.
fix: जिसकी कृपासे तू बहुत पुण्य और दान करता है, हे मन! आठों पहर उसका ध्यान कर। जिसकी कृपासे तू धर्म-आचार और व्यवहार करता है, उस प्रभुको श्वास-श्वास याद कर। जिसकी कृपासे तेरा सुन्दर रूप है, उस अनुपम प्रभुका सदा स्मरण करो। जिसकी कृपासे तेरी अच्छी जाति (ऊँचा कुल) है, उस प्रभुको सदा दिन-रात याद कर। जिसकी कृपासे तेरी प्रतिष्ठा बनी रहती है, गुरुकी कृपासे नानक उसका यश कहता है।
